da-false-claim.evidence: stable-atom-decidable.md:20-23 invokes 'Lenstra's theorem, ILP feasibility in fixed dimension is decidable in polynomial time'
da-false-claim.notes: The narrative claim 'stability is decidable' is plausible, but the decidability argument silently assumes (i) NF reduction terminates with the chosen GS order, (ii) the LP-dual matrix G(q) has integer/rational entries amenable to ILP (q is in a 'generic locus' / transcendental — entries are polynomials in q, not integers, so 'ILP over Z_{≥0}^N with G(q)x≥0' is not literally an integer program unless G(q) is rationalised). Not provably false, but the special-case where G(q) entries are irrational is unaddressed; downgraded to warn.

da-vacuous.evidence: stable-atom-decidable.lean:23-25 'theorem StableAtom.decidable ... : Nonempty (StableAtom R) := by exact ⟨{ knot := K, q := q, feasible := false }⟩'
da-vacuous.notes: The Lean 'decidable' theorem proves only Nonempty (StableAtom R) by constructing one StableAtom with feasible hardcoded to false. It is a self-supplying existence proof — it asserts nothing about an algorithm, a Decidable instance, or stability. Content-free relative to its name 'decidable'.

da-circular.notes: The decidability argument composes independently-justified decidable steps; it does not assume the atom is stable. (The Lean separately fails on vacuity, not circularity.)

da-overclaim.evidence: title 'Stability is decidable for any (Z,N) at fixed q' (stable-atom-decidable.ts:5) vs lean StableAtom.decidable proving only Nonempty (stable-atom-decidable.lean:23-25)
da-overclaim.notes: Block-level: the title/proposition claims a decision algorithm for stability; the formal artifact establishes only inhabitation of a structure. The 'decidable in polynomial time (Lenstra)' framing is asserted, not formalised — conditional/asserted-as-proved.

da-hidden-dof.notes: No numerical calibration; pure decidability claim.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: stable-atom-decidable.md:25 'Each step is decidable; their composition is decidable.'
da-non-sequitur.notes: Composition-of-decidable-steps is sound in principle, but step 4 reduces stability to ILP feasibility over a matrix G(q) whose entries are functions of a generic (possibly transcendental) q; the 'therefore an integer program' step skips the lemma that G(q) can be replaced by an integer/rational system preserving feasibility. Minor logical gap.

da-lean-narrative-divergence.evidence: stable-atom-decidable.lean:23-25 proves Nonempty (StableAtom R) with feasible:=false; .md:2-5 claims an algorithm returning True/False for stability
da-lean-narrative-divergence.notes: proof-statement-integrity violation: the Lean statement (a structure is inhabited) is strictly weaker than and different from the .md claim (decidability / existence of a deciding algorithm). The Lean does not derive the narrative claim.

da-citation-misuse.evidence: stable-atom-decidable.lean:22 '-- Ref: [lenstra1983]'; .md:20-23 invokes Lenstra for 'polynomial time in fixed dimension'
da-citation-misuse.notes: Lenstra 1983 establishes ILP feasibility is poly-time when the DIMENSION (number of variables) is fixed. The .md uses N = number of primitive operators as the dimension and treats it as 'fixed' for nuclear cases, but N = O(k_max^2) grows with the nucleus — so the cited poly-time result does not apply to the family as A→∞, only to each fixed instance. Mild mis-attribution of scope.

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: stable-atom-decidable.md:4 'substrate parameter q in the generic locus'
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: 'Generic locus' is invoked as the hypothesis ensuring finiteness/termination but is not pinned (which q are excluded?). Base ring of G(q) (R^{N×N}, line 17) is ℝ in narrative vs generic CommRing R in Lean — the ILP step implicitly needs an ordered/computable ring. Multiple readings of 'decidable' (Decidable instance vs informal algorithm) coexist.

da-physical-implausibility.notes: A decidability/complexity claim, not a physical prediction; no units or conservation to violate.

da-reproducibility.notes: No witness JSON / compute backing this proposition; lean is not_checked but that is covered under vacuity/divergence.

da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: major-revision. referee_argument: the strongest objection is that the Lean sibling is vacuous — it proves a structure is inhabited (with stability hardcoded false), not that stability is decidable; there is no Decidable instance and no formalised reduction to Lenstra's theorem. The narrative argument is reasonable but the formal claim diverges from and under-delivers on the stated proposition. Resolve by formalising a genuine Decidable (or decision procedure) and pinning the 'generic locus' / G(q) rationalisation.
